The files in this folder hold wind data of the OpenWindMap wind network
(formerly Pioupiou), measured by sensors that pilots, clubs and schools put
up, and published under the network's Community License,
https://developers.pioupiou.fr/data-licensing/:

    Wind data (c) contributors of the OpenWindMap wind network
    <https://openwindmap.org>

They are not covered by the licence of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-22 from https://api.pioupiou.fr/v1/, without
a key, with curl.

live_all.json is the answer to the adapter's one request,

    GET /live/all   asked at 08:09:00 UTC (the answer's Date header:
                    08:09:02 GMT), 462,653 bytes, 763 sensors

cut down to sixteen of its sensors. The answer is JSON indented by two
spaces with non-ASCII characters escaped, which Python's
json.dumps(answer, indent=2) reproduces byte for byte: the cut was made by
reading the answer, keeping the head ("doc", "license", "attribution") and
the sixteen entries of "data" in their order, unchanged, and writing it out
in the same way. The sixteen, by id:

    in the Alps' western box (5.0 to 9.4 E, 43.5 to 48.5 N), with a reading
    of wind: 69, 70 (Salève), 1343 (Nendaz), 1359 (Felci), 1708 (Anglettaz),
    1724 (Planpraz); switched off, with a reading of 8 November: 1592, and
    1635, whose reading has no maximum
    in the box without a reading of wind: 123, 1720 (Doussard)
    in the box, its position "no longer valid" by the network: 1602
    without a latitude: 2392; at 0, 0: 916
    outside the box: 41 (Gers), 1514 (Kampenwand), 2077 (Osterfelder)

The whole answer had, inside the Alps' box (5.0 to 17.2 E, 43.5 to 48.5
N), 369 sensors, 309 of them with a reading of the last ten minutes; 304 in
the western box and 45 in the first region's (9.4 to 17.2 E, 46.3 to
48.5 N). 62 of the 763 had a position the network calls no longer valid,
2 none, and 38 no reading of wind.

The folder evening/ holds three answers of the network's archive, whole
and unchanged, asked at 08:10:30 UTC:

    evening/ID.json   GET /archive/ID?start=2026-11-18T18:30Z
                      &stop=2026-11-18T19:10Z

for the sensors 1514 (Kampenwand Hirschenstein), 2077 (Osterfelder Nord)
and 2150 (Coburgerhütte): their readings between 18:30 and 19:10 UTC on
2026-11-18, eight each. The adapter does not ask the archive. They are here
for the next file.

live_evening.json is NOT an answer of the network as it gave it. It is a
sample for the server's development mode, whose clock stands at 19:05 UTC
on 2026-11-18, four days before this source was recorded; the live answer
holds the newest reading only. It is the head of the answer of 2026-11-22
and the entries of the three sensors above from it, written as above, with
in each: location.latitude and location.longitude, measurements.date,
wind_speed_min, wind_speed_avg, wind_speed_max, wind_heading and pressure
replaced by the last row of evening/ID.json before 19:05 UTC, and
location.date and status.date set to that row's time. So every value of
wind and every position in the sample is one the network gave, for the
sensor and the moment the sample says. What the live answer was at that
moment is not known. A test of this crate holds the sample against the
archive.

live_empty.json is the head of the answer with an empty "data", written by
hand: the network was not seen to answer so.

live_damaged.json is not the network's data: it is live_evening.json with
five things changed by hand, to test how the adapter reports what it
cannot read. The test that uses it says what was changed.

To record them again: fetch /live/all, cut it down as above (the counts
the test pins are of the sixteen sensors and of that moment), set the
moment in tests/pipeline.rs, run the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and
review what changed. The evening sample stays as it is for as long as the
development mode's clock does.

A value in these files is what an instrument reported. It is no statement
that a place can be flown.
